events.title: Theodosius I defeats Eugenius at the Frigidus
events.description: Emperor Theodosius defeated the usurper Eugenius, backed by the pagan senatorial aristocracy, in a two-day battle in the Julian Alps. Traditional Roman religion lost its last political champion.
events.html: Emperor Theodosius defeated the usurper Eugenius, backed by the pagan senatorial aristocracy, in a two-day battle in the Julian Alps. Traditional Roman religion lost its last political champion.

events.title: The Victoria completes the first voyage around the world
events.description: The Victoria, last survivor of Magellan's five ships, reached Spain under Juan Sebastián Elcano with 18 men. The voyage revealed the vast size of the Pacific and the true scale of the globe.
events.html: The Victoria, last survivor of Magellan's five ships, reached Spain under Juan Sebastián Elcano with 18 men. The voyage revealed the vast size of the Pacific and the true scale of the globe.

events.title: John Endecott's Puritans arrive at Salem
events.description: John Endecott landed at Naumkeag with Puritan settlers, taking charge of the small settlement soon renamed Salem. It became the first town of the Massachusetts Bay Colony.
events.html: John Endecott landed at Naumkeag with Puritan settlers, taking charge of the small settlement soon renamed Salem. It became the first town of the Massachusetts Bay Colony.

events.title: President McKinley is shot in Buffalo
events.description: Anarchist Leon Czolgosz shot William McKinley twice at the Pan-American Exposition. The president died eight days later, and Theodore Roosevelt succeeded him.
events.html: Anarchist Leon Czolgosz shot William McKinley twice at the Pan-American Exposition. The president died eight days later, and Theodore Roosevelt succeeded him.

events.title: Hendrik Verwoerd is stabbed to death in parliament
events.description: South Africa's prime minister, chief architect of apartheid, was killed in the House of Assembly in Cape Town by parliamentary messenger Dimitri Tsafendas. Apartheid continued under his successors.
events.html: South Africa's prime minister, chief architect of apartheid, was killed in the House of Assembly in Cape Town by parliamentary messenger Dimitri Tsafendas. Apartheid continued under his successors.
